title: feat(043): the driver seam, the engine loses its provider-specific contract
body:
## Summary

Authors and implements spec 043 (doc 02 §8's next step after 042 and statecraft-cli 008), `status: approved` per this corpus's habit (D-6).

- **One seam** `src/orchestrator/driver.ts`: a provider-neutral request on the driver member's stdin, a line-delimited event stream on its stdout (`journal` / `stream` / `result`), a `SessionResult` at the end. The engine appends the forwarded `journal` events, so `session.init` and `session.result` carry spec 014's payloads byte for byte (asserted in-process vs through the seam).
- **The member side** `statecraft-driver-claude session run` wraps `runSession` unchanged; exit 0 for any session outcome (quota, timeout included), 3 for a bad request, 1 for a driver failure. SIGTERM forwards to the provider child through 014's own path.
- **Discovery** mirrors statecraft-cli 008: `STATECRAFT_DRIVER_BIN`, then `STATECRAFT_MEMBER_DIR`, the platform data dir, `PATH`, then (from a checkout) the member entrypoint under bun.
- **Tier consumed** (042 B-8): a `basic` driver asked for an MCP server set is never spawned; `driver.degraded` is journaled and the browser verifier reports the assertion as not passed.
- **Everything drives through it**: build runner (shared by ship and shepherd), browser verifier, daemon, standby shutdown, synthesis sessions, CLI.
- **D-7** spec 040's default model pair moves to the driver; the engine passes a tier. `projects` renders a project with no pair as `(driver default)`.
- **D-8** the dispatcher leaves `src/index.ts` for `src/members/dispatch.ts` (a function over a verb table, no verb imports): the first engine build carried the driver's `models` verb and its ids. Each member now bundles only what it claims; 042 FR-003's byte-identity holds unchanged.
- **FR-005** `engine-bundle.test.ts`: the compiled engine contains none of `stream-json`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--permission-mode`, `claude-opus`, `claude-sonnet`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; the compiled driver contains all of them.

## Verification

- `bun test src/orchestrator/driver.test.ts src/members/`: 39 pass (FR-001 to FR-005, B-3 byte-identity, B-5 discovery order, kill and deadline paths)
- `bun test`: 831 pass, 11 fail. The 11 fail identically on `main` under a local spec-spine 0.18.0 (its `init` writes `AGENTS.md`, which 035's corpus-set guard refuses); CI's 0.15.0 does not hit this. Worth a `fix(035)` follow-up.
- `bun run typecheck` clean; 0.15.0 `lint --fail-on-warn` clean; `index check` fresh; `couple` OK on 24 paths through additive `extends` edges (no waiver).
- **AC-5 live**: from the checkout, `createProcessDriver()` discovered the driver member, read its manifest, drove one fast-tier turn of Claude Code 2.1.266 to completion (1 turn, 51827 micro-USD), and `verifyChain` reported the journaled chain intact.

title: docs(design): 02, record the canonicalization check and the defect it found
body:
Doc 02 §9 listed the `stableStringify` versus `canonical-keysort-json`
comparison as its one open gate on D30's journal port. This records the
result. Docs only; `couple` reports 0 paths checked.

## The corpus agrees, completely

All 1,696 work records and 70 decision records were recomputed **from the
original `.jsonl` bytes with no JavaScript in the path**: parsed with
`serde_json`, canonicalized through `canonical-keysort-json`, hashed with
sha256, compared to the stored `recordHash`.

```
work journal      total=1696 verified=1696 mismatched=0
decision ledger   total=70   verified=70   mismatched=0
```

Comparing canonical output directly, `stableStringify` and
`to_canonical_string` are byte-identical over 695,206 bytes. The committed
bundle also still verifies under the shipped verifier (both chains intact,
1038 work and 52 decision records).

So the journal port is mechanical for every record written so far.

## The check also found a defect here, not in the port

`canonicalizeValue` sorts keys lexicographically and inserts them into a
plain object. JavaScript enumerates array-index-like keys (canonical decimal
integers in `[0, 2**32-2]`) **first, in ascending numeric order, regardless
of insertion order**, so for those keys the sort is silently discarded:

```
{"9":_,"10":_,"2":_}   lexicographic want: ["10","2","9"]
                       actually emitted:   ["2","9","10"]
```

The function's header states a "recursive lexicographic key-sort" and for
this class of key that does not hold. The existing chain is unaffected
because the writer and the verifier share the behavior, which is exactly why
it has gone unnoticed: it is invisible to everything except a second
implementation. `canonical-keysort-json` sorts by UTF-8 bytes and has no
such carve-out.

A scan of all 1,810 available records, the bundle included, finds **zero**
objects that would trigger it. It is latent, not active.

## Three narrower divergences, also recorded

- **Lone surrogate.** `JSON.stringify` emits `\udXXX`; `serde_json` refuses
  to parse it. More plausible here than it looks: the journal carries agent
  output, and a truncated stream can split a surrogate pair.
- **Integers above 2^53.** JavaScript parses them lossily and silently,
  since `Number.isInteger` passes after the precision is already gone.
- **Number shapes.** The Rust crate accepts floats `journal.ts` rejects by
  design, and re-emits `1e2` as `100.0` and `-0` as `-0.0`. Only reachable
  through foreign input, since `JSON.stringify` never writes those forms.

## What it changes for D30

The journal gate is no longer only "reproduce the stored hashes", which now
passes. It is also "decide which lexicographic order is the canonical one"
before a second implementation exists, because the two currently define
different canonical forms for a class of input the corpus does not yet
contain.

Changing `journal.ts` is a change to shipped behavior owned by spec 011, so
it is named here and deliberately not fixed in passing.

title: docs(design): 02, the monorepo and the Rust sequence
body:
Design doc 02, recording D24 through D30. Succeeds doc 01 and supersedes
its D14. No code changes; `couple` reports 0 paths checked.

## What it decides

**D24, the host (amends 01 D14).** `statecraft-cli` becomes the monorepo
for the family's tooling, daemons and CLI packages, and this repository's
three members move into it. D14's reasoning is retained: the repo split and
the binary split are independent decisions. The repo one is now taken, with
the opposite host from the one D14 assumed. The boundary is stated
explicitly, because a monorepo with no stated edge absorbs everything:
`statecraft`, `rahi`, `spec-spine` and the four frozen substrate crates
stay outside and are consumed as dependencies.

**D25, the process boundary survives the merge.** Members stay separate
processes even though one repository makes collapsing them easy. The
boundary is what lets members be written in different languages at the same
time (which is what makes the Rust question a sequence instead of a flag
day), what allows a third-party driver to exist, and what 042 B-6 and 008
D-5 already specify. The merge's actual payment is narrower and better: the
member contract stops being prose in two corpora that both declare a
divergence "a defect in both", and becomes a crate both sides depend on, so
divergence is a compile error.

**D26, the provider axis.** For N providers the member count is 2N+1, so
the sensor and driver families each split into a provider-neutral core and
a thin per-provider crate. `classify.ts` is already a pattern-to-event
table over an observed root, so a Codex or Cursor sensor costs a table and
a path, not a second watcher, event store and redaction path.

**D27, naming.** "Observatory" retires with the repository rather than
being replaced: after the split there is no unit it names. Binary names
stay as 042 B-1 and 008 §3 fixed them, since those are the umbrella's
discovery keys. Internal crates take the `statecraft-` prefix. Verb-surface
flattening stays deferred per 042 D-7, and the repository rename waits
until cross-references are no longer in flight.

**D28, the corpus merge direction.** statecraft-cli's specs renumber to
101-108; this repository's 000-042 import unchanged. Measured: exactly one
literal id collision (`000-bootstrap`) and nine ordinal collisions, none of
which spec-spine would refuse, since 053's monotonicity lint is opt-in and
defaults off. The direction is not chosen by counting specs: this
repository's ids are written into the work journal, the decision ledger and
`docs/evidence/journal-bundle.json`, where a renumber either invalidates
the chains or leaves the bundle's ids naming nothing.

**D29 and D30, Rust.** Adopted as a sequence, not a rewrite. No spec called
"rewrite in Rust" and no flag day; each member ports behind the 042
contract, proved by AC-4's byte-identical output requirement against the
implementation it replaces. Order: contract crate, sensor, then journal and
export (gated on re-verifying the existing bundle byte for byte), then the
engine only if the first two prove the ergonomics. The Claude driver may
stay TypeScript, since a polyglot driver family is the strongest available
evidence that the seam is real.

## Measurements behind it

The strongest Rust argument is recorded with its evidence:
`src/orchestrator/journal.ts:9` states it implements the attest-ledger
record chain with canonical key-sorted JSON, both of which are published
Rust crates. Two independent canonical-JSON implementations sit underneath
a product whose claim is offline-verifiable tamper-evident chains.

Also measured and cited: 22,026 production TypeScript lines against 18,423
test lines and 3,770 lines of React that do not move; `Bun.spawn` in 12
non-test files, `Bun.serve` in 2, `bun:sqlite` in 1; the watcher on node's
`fs.watch` rather than a Bun API; no runtime npm dependencies.

§9 lists what was not verified, including the one check that should precede
any port: whether `stableStringify` and `canonical-keysort-json` agree byte
for byte on the records already written.

## Also recorded

§1 records the base-branch defect that stranded doc 01 and spec 042 off
trunk for a day (#71 and #72 merged into `chore-spec-spine-0-15-0`, which
had already landed as #70, recovered by #73). Neither CI nor the coupling
gate can see that a green PR landed on a branch that no longer leads
anywhere.

title: feat(specs): author 042 member-contract, the shape the umbrella dispatches to
body:
Stacked on #71 (design doc 01), which is its `references:` target. Rebase to
`main` once #71 merges.

## Summary

Design doc 01 D13/D14 split this repository into three members behind one
umbrella CLI. Spec 042 is the packaging and protocol half of that move, and
deliberately not the refactor: three build targets, the manifest each member
declares itself with, and the output contract the umbrella dispatches against,
with nothing moved between layers. The engine stays internally Claude-aware
until 043.

The split between 042 and 043 exists because packaging is mechanically
falsifiable (a build target either produces a binary or it does not) and
because both in one spec would exceed a single driven session's territory,
which is the bound this corpus holds every spec to. AC-3 and AC-5 are the
teeth: every test written before this spec must still pass unedited, and the
diff must touch nothing under `src/` outside `src/members/` and `src/index.ts`.

## Authored as draft, and why

Two collisions between already-shipped contracts turned up while writing it.
`.claude/rules/adversarial-prompt-refusal.md` reserves that class of call for a
human, so the spec is `status: draft` and ratification is a separate commit.

**D-2 amends doc 01 D17.** The doc said members emit spec-spine's 037 verdict
envelope. They should not: spec 023 B-3 and statecraft-cli spec 004 §5.2
already specify the same `{ok, data|error}` shape, and
`src/orchestrator/api/types.ts:8` states outright that the envelope "follows
statecraft-cli's own output pattern". D17 invented a divergence that does not
exist. spec-spine's 037 envelope is what its own gate verbs emit and stays
that.

**D-3 resolves the exit-code collision by declaring it, not remapping it.**
Spec 023 D-4 reads `2` as an unreachable daemon and `3` as usage. The
umbrella's clap hardcodes `2` as usage and statecraft-cli spec 004 already
documents "a missing base URL is usage (exit 2)". Remapping at the dispatch
boundary was rejected because it makes `statecraft engine status` and
`statecraft-engine status` disagree, breaking every script that calls a member
directly and contradicting doc 01 D18. Changing 023's taxonomy was rejected
because it is shipped, tested, and asserted by 023's own verification block.
Adopted: codes pass through verbatim, each member declares its taxonomy in its
manifest, and the umbrella's dispatch failures move to 64 and above. The
residue is stated rather than hidden, and the manifest is what makes it
discoverable.

A third correction landed during authoring: `verbs` was briefly the top-level
dispatch key, which collides between members and with umbrella built-ins. The
dispatch key is now the member's `name`, so two members may both offer a
`status` without either shadowing anything.

The umbrella half is statecraft-cli spec 008, authored in the same session and
citing this one. Neither is the authority over the other; a divergence between
them is a defect in both.

## Testing

- `spec-spine compile`: 42 specs, 0 warnings.
- `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info.
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh. `index diagnostics` reports 6 `W-001`, one
  per file unit this spec claims before it is built. That is the ratified-
  before-built case spec-spine's own specs 025 and 044 exist to allow; it is
  warning tier and the gate stays green.
- `spec-spine couple --base origin/main --head HEAD`: no drift.
- `spec-spine registry plan`: `ready: 1, blocked: 0`.

No source changed, so no typecheck or test delta.

title: docs(design): the umbrella CLI and the three member seams
body:
## Summary

Adds `docs/design/01-umbrella-cli-and-member-seams.md`, the successor to
`00-ecosystem-analysis.md`. It records the architecture for turning this
repository into a family of member binaries behind a single `statecraft` CLI,
and it corrects three premises of 00 that no longer hold.

Decision numbering continues 00's sequence: 00 owns D1-D12, this document owns
D13-D23.

**What changed since 00**

- statecraft's base is rahi, not enrahitu. rahi is not a plan: six crates,
  18,427 lines of Rust, ten specs complete and one in flight, built by this
  repository's own orchestrator.
- The hosted control plane moves behind the local product.
- 00's D11 kept the name `claude-observatory` and treated the orchestrator as a
  capability of the observatory. That is superseded: the user-facing name is
  `statecraft`, and this repo's parts become members behind it.

**The split**, per seam rather than one lift-and-shift binary, so a second
driver drops in beside the first: `statecraft-sensor-claude` (specs 001-008),
`statecraft-engine` (010-013, 015-039, 041), `statecraft-driver-claude`
(014, 040).

Two measured facts make it cheap. The driver boundary is already a process
boundary: `src/orchestrator/session.ts` spawns a configurable `claudeBin` with
`-p --output-format stream-json --verbose`, prompt on stdin and never on argv,
and parses a JSON stream off its stdout. And the coupling to extract is
concentrated: `claude` appears in 14 non-test files under `src/orchestrator/`,
with 47 of the mentions in four of them.

**The gap in the umbrella is precise.** statecraft-cli at M4 already has the
command tree, an MCP stdio face, a JSON error envelope and tag-gated releases.
But every verb it owns is a client of a hosted control plane through `api.rs`
and `auth.rs`. There is no local-execution verb and no notion of a member, so
D20 specifies the dispatch path as account-less: the local loop never requires
`statecraft login`.

**Superseded from 00**, each needing a recorded amendment in its owning spec
before code moves: D6 (session driving becomes the driver's contract, mechanics
intact), D9 (hook-blocked stays terminal but becomes driver-reported), D10
(verify by Chrome is a richest-tier driver capability, not an engine
requirement), D11 (naming, superseded outright).

**Spec plan:** 042 and 043 here, 008 and 009 in statecraft-cli. 042 and 008 are
the pair that must agree across two corpora with two coupling gates, so they are
written together.

## Testing

Documentation only; no source, spec, schema or workflow inputs changed.

- `spec-spine compile`: 41 specs, 0 warnings.
- `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info.
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh.
- `spec-spine couple --base origin/main --head HEAD`: no drift.

Every load-bearing claim was verified on disk rather than carried over from an
earlier survey, which caught two errors in the first draft: the doc had repeated
rahi's own stale README claim of being unbuilt, and it cited "spec 037" for the
verdict envelope, which collides with this corpus's defect-capture 037. Both are
fixed. The envelope shape in D17 was confirmed live against
`spec-spine index check --json` and `spec-spine verify --json` at 0.15.0.

Three items are recorded as explicitly unverified rather than assumed:
fleet-native's contents, whether statecraft's deployment is green, and whether
the rahi run is live, parked or disarmed.

title: feat(orchestrator): a driven target is judged by its own language gate (spec 041)
body:
## Summary

- Makes the post-session language gate per-project registry state instead of this repo's hardcoded conventions. A gate contract is an ordered argv list plus who set it, folded off the projects chain exactly as the execution profile is (spec 032's shape applied to spec 016 D-10's gap).
- Registration probes the target read-only, first matching rule wins: a `Makefile` with a `ci` target, then `tsconfig.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, a `pyproject.toml`'s declared tool tables, else the empty contract. The rule that fired is journaled, so a governance-only gate says why.
- `gateSuiteFor()` is now the only source of a stage's gate list; `gateCommandsFor(runner)` and its per-run tsconfig probe are gone. The build stage's preflight, its post-session evidence, and shepherd's remediation prompt all read the same suite, so a Rust target is told to run cargo rather than bun.

title: fix(orchestrator): the decision capture path stops losing what sessions decide (016 D-11..D-13, 020 D-6, D-7)
body:
## Summary

Five defects on the path between a driven session and the decision ledger,
every one of them found live on butler-ai, where they cost four sessions and
\$17.44 to prove a wall that did not exist, plus \$3.16 re-deriving one
coupling violation verbatim.

- **016 D-11 / 020 D-7, the drop-box contract is typed.** The prompt named
  the record shape and left every type to be guessed. 25 of 25 butler-ai
  decisions across four sessions wrote `"scope": "reducer"` where 020 B-1
  defines a list; every one was rejected and `decisions.jsonl` was still 0
  bytes after a full spec had been built. The loss is silent to the session
  and compounding, because B-4's injection then has nothing to inject. The
  prompt now gives the type of every field, says `scope` is an array and
  never a bare string, says a rejected record reaches neither the ledger nor
  a later session, and carries a complete copyable example built from the
  spec's own id. On the validator side, an explicit `null` on an optional
  field now reads as absent rather than as a malformed value; three more
  butler-ai decisions were discarded over `"supersedes": null`. Null is
  normalized away at construction so it can never reach the canonical
  payload the content hash is taken over.

- **016 D-12, the prompt teaches `extends`.** The prompt told sessions which
  gate commands must exit 0 and never how to satisfy the one that cannot be
  satisfied by writing code. Sessions correctly refused to amend the owning
  spec and correctly ruled out a waiver by experiment, then concluded no
  branch-side fix existed. They were wrong: one declared `extends` entry took
  `couple` from 1 to 0. The prompt now states the mechanism and both
  forbidden answers, and states the case where `extends` is wrong, so it
  never becomes a way to declare away a real contradiction.

- **016 D-13, a stalled stage stops asking.** When the remediation session
  leaves the branch head untouched and the gate answers identically, tails
  included, the stage has asked the same question twice against unchanged
  inputs. `BuildEvidence.stalled` carries that judgment (null when no
  remediation ran, so "not asked" is never read as "not stalled"), and the
  daemon pauses on it instead of spending the retry budget on a third and
  fourth session. This narrows what the retry budget is for: a flaky failure,
  not a deterministic one.

- **020 D-6, a rejection is reported once.** An invalid file preserved in
  place is re-read, re-rejected and re-reported by every later sweep forever;
  eight butler-ai files rejected on 2026-09-01 were still in every build's
  report two days later. Preserved now means moved to an `invalid/`
  subdirectory, created lazily. Because the drop-box is one directory shared
  by every spec and every attempt, a repeated basename takes the first free
  numeric suffix rather than replacing the file already there.

`BUILD_PROMPT_VERSION` goes to 2 in the same change: the version is journaled
with every use, so holding it at 1 across a changed template would leave
`stage.build.prompt` unable to answer which text a session actually saw.

## Testing

Full local gate, all green:

- `spec-spine compile`: 41 specs, 0 warnings
- `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh
- `spec-spine couple --base origin/main --head HEAD`: OK, 9 paths, no drift
- `bun run typecheck`: clean
- `bun test`: 758 pass, 0 fail

Eight new tests cover the decisions directly: the typed prompt and its
copyable array-scope example, the `extends` instruction, null-as-absent and
the still-rejected wrong type, a second sweep no longer seeing a file it
already reported, both files surviving a repeated basename, stalled true /
false / null across the three remediation outcomes, and the daemon pausing on
the stall signal while still spending its budget on a failure without one.

title: feat(specs): author 041 project-gate-contract, per-project language gates as registry state
body:
## Summary

The post-session gate a driven target is judged by is this repo's own: four
`spec-spine` commands plus `bun run typecheck` and `bun test`, with the Bun
pair dropped whenever the target has no root `tsconfig.json` (016 D-10). A
Rust target therefore passes the build stage on governance alone. Cargo
correctness reaches the pipeline only through whatever the session ran for
itself, which is the self-authored evidence 016 exists to refuse, and through
CI in the shepherd stage. rahi records this as its spec 001 D-1 and works
around it by having the session run `make ci`. With rahi, aicortex and hqgit
all Rust and all pending arming, that gap is a claim the orchestrator makes
without evidence.

041 makes the language gate per-project registry state, following 032 exactly:
a journaled `project.gate.set` contract folded off the projects chain, probed
at registration, derived into the stage suite by one pure function every stage
uses, and rendered wherever the project is named. The universal `spec-spine`
floor stays 016's and always runs.

The probe ladder, first match wins:

| # | evidence in the target root | commands |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Makefile` with a `ci` target | `make ci` |
| 2 | `tsconfig.json` | `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` |
| 3 | `Cargo.toml` | `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked` |
| 4 | `go.mod` | `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` |
| 5 | `pyproject.toml` | the declared tools only (D-4) |
| 6 | none | governance-only |

Spec only. No code changes; `implementation: pending`, for the daemon to build.

### Review findings fixed before opening

Reviewing the authored draft found the legacy fold inverting the spec's own
purpose. B-3 folded a project with no gate record to "the Bun pair if the
registration record carries `hasTsconfig`, else empty". Journal records are
immutable, so no pre-041 registration can carry that field, and all six
registered projects predate the spec. `claude-observatory` is the only one
with a language gate today, and it would have silently dropped to
governance-only, leaving the repo the orchestrator builds itself with judged
without typecheck or tests. rahi would have stayed governance-only despite its
`make ci` target, defeating the reason to land this before arming it.

B-8 closes the window: the first time the daemon services a project with no
gate record, it runs the probe and appends one. The probe runs at write time,
so the fold stays a pure function of the chain (D-2 untouched) and the
record's existence is the idempotence guard. `hasTsconfig` is gone and D-2
records why it never worked.

Two coupling defects were also fixed in the authored spec: the API `extends`
edge was a bare directory unit, which no spec has ever carried through
`couple` (032's build proved the file-level form works), and four colocated
test edges its own FR-005 requires were missing, including the two `web/test/`
edges that keep the dashboard's typecheck green when the served payload gains
a field.

## Testing

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `spec-spine compile` | 41 specs, 0 warnings |
| `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn` | 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info |
| `spec-spine index check` | fresh |
| `spec-spine couple --base origin/main --head HEAD` | OK, 1 path, no drift |

Probe rules were checked against the live registry: `claude-observatory`
matches rule 2, `tenant-emit` / `tenant-tail` / `icebeek` rule 3, `rahi` rule
1, `butler-ai` rule 6. AC-5 asserts that outcome on the real registry after
migration, rather than on a fixture alone.

title: feat(orchestrator): driven sessions run on a model that was chosen (spec 040)
body:
Spec 014 has always accepted an optional model and appended `--model` when one
was given. Nothing ever gave one. Every driven session ran on whatever the CLI
resolved by default at spawn time, and the field that would have recorded it
stayed null for all 44 sessions the journal holds. The transcripts of the
butler-ai run show 548 assistant turns on a model no part of this system
selected.

## What changed

- **`src/orchestrator/models.ts`**, the counterpart of 032's `profile.ts`.
  `modelForStage()` is the only place a `--model` value is produced (B-1), and
  the stage-to-tier map is `Record<Stage, ModelTier>`, so a stage added to
  013's machine without a tier does not compile (FR-002).
- **Tiers follow difficulty, not order.** Build and ship take the strong
  model; shepherd and verify take the fast one. The last 43 journaled sessions
  were 33 shepherd and verify against 10 build and ship, so the cheap tier
  covers most of the volume without touching the two stages where quality is
  load-bearing (D-1).
- **Defaults are `claude-opus-5` and `claude-sonnet-5`**, deliberately not the
  long-context ids. `opus[1m]` is this machine's interactive default, and
  inheriting it is how headless sessions were paying long-context rates (D-4).
- **A project may carry its own pair**, journaled on its execution profile and
  folded exactly as the posture is. No second chain, no second verb (D-2).
  Both halves or neither, with a refusal that names the missing one (D-3).
- **`session.init` records the model it spawned under.** The field stops being
  null, so a run can be reproduced rather than guessed at.

The verify stage spawns no session of its own: its only model session belongs
to the browser verifier, which already resolves the project's profile at that
seam, so the verify tier resolves there too (D-6). That is why three stage
options carry a model and four stages are covered.

## Gate

`compile` 40 specs / 0 warnings; `lint --fail-on-warn` 0/0/0; `index check`
fresh; `couple --base origin/main --head HEAD` 10 paths / no drift;
`bun run typecheck` clean; `bun test` 747 pass / 0 fail.

## Acceptance

- **AC-1** daemon test drives the pipeline with recording stage functions and
  asserts build and ship on strong, shepherd on fast.
- **AC-2** the journaled posture test now carries a non-null model.
- **AC-3/AC-4** CLI tests: the default pair renders marked as default, the

title: fix(api): a tick between stream closes and stop(true) frees SIGTERM (022 D-10)
body:
## Summary

Root-causes and fixes the intermittent 026 B-7 violation (SIGTERM in standby ignored, SIGKILL needed, observed 2026-08-06).

On Bun 1.3.11, closing two or more stream controllers and calling `server.stop(true)` in the same event-loop turn leaves that promise forever pending, even though every socket and the listener are torn down at the OS level (lsof shows zero fds; only the promise leaks). `ApiServer.stop()` performed exactly that sequence, and the daemon's signal handler awaits it before anything else while latching its re-entry guard, so the leaked promise made the process deaf to every subsequent TERM while the scheduler loop kept running.

The hidden second client that made it look intermittent: an open dashboard tab auto-reconnects its SSE stream within seconds of every daemon boot. One tab alone (one stream) stops cleanly; the tab plus any second client (a curl, another tab) crosses the two-stream threshold and hung every time.

The fix is one yielded tick (`await Bun.sleep(0)`) between the controller closes and the force-stop, recorded as 022 D-10 with the residual risk named.

## Testing

- Generic repro outside the repo isolates the Bun defect: 1 stream resolves, >=2 streams closed in the same turn as `stop(true)` hang, a tick in between resolves (5/5 each way).
- Live daemon cycles pre-fix: 4/4 hangs with an SSE client attached (second TERM swallowed, native sample shows an idle event loop waiting on the leaked promise), 0.28 s clean stops without.
- Live daemon post-fix: clean 0.28 s stop with eight SSE/keep-alive clients attached (six Chrome dashboard connections plus two curls), "standby stopped" journaled.
- New regression test holds two streams open and races `stop()` against a bound; verified to fail with the fix removed.
- `spec-spine compile | lint --fail-on-warn | index check | couple` green (couple: 3 paths, no drift); full suite 735 pass.

title: fix(daemon): journaled controls survive restarts; status tells current truth
body:
## Summary

Four operational-honesty fixes found while working the first family-repo build, each coupled to its owning spec:

- **Durable controls (021 D-24, 026 D-11).** A control accepted by the API is now a durable promise of the project's chain. Every issue journals `restorable: true` with its record seq; applying one (including a state-conditional no-op apply) journals `control.applied` keyed to that seq; recovery replays restorable-but-unapplied controls at any open, in journal order, with one `daemon.controls.restored` summary. Pre-fix records lack the marker and never re-fire (a consumed-but-unmarked control cannot be told from an unconsumed one). Standby-auto reverifies are excluded (the next scan re-derives them from drift), and `concludeIdle()` refuses while restored controls sit queued so a probe drives them through exactly once. Found live three times over: tenant-tail's bootstrap retry died with its daemon on every restart.
- **Refusal-carrying pause reasons (021 D-25).** A blocked stage's pause reason appends the build refusal's kind and message (bounded to 400 chars): `status` now answers "why is it paused right now" (found live: a `gate-red-at-base` pause that read only as `build outcome "refused"`).
- **Run-scoped blockers (027 D-9).** The run view surfaces `run.blocked` only while its `runId` is the latest run's; a dead run's "status draft is not approved" verdict no longer renders beside a current pause that says something else.
- **Honest terminal rows (028 D-11).** A completed or failed run's row drops the spec/stage suffix that read as work in flight (`completed  033-cost-ceiling/build`). 028 also gains the establishes edge for its own colocated test file, which the graph expected (035/036's extends edges already name it) but never carried.
- **Deliberate SSE lifetime (022 D-9).** `Bun.serve` runs with `idleTimeout: 0`: the default 10 s timeout's only observed effect was severing quiet SSE streams and logging `[Bun.serve]: request timed out` noise on each kill.

## Testing

- New tests: controls survive a daemon death and apply exactly once, with a third open restoring nothing; pre-fix unmarked records never re-fire; `concludeIdle` refuses over queued controls; the standby end-to-end replay of the tenant-tail wound (journaled retry + dead daemon + recovered pause heals and builds); refusal detail in the journaled pause reason; blockers scoped to the stopping run; the terminal-row cell.
- Full suite at prep time: 708 pass, 0 fail; compile / index / lint --fail-on-warn / index check green; couple: 13 paths, no drift; typecheck clean.

title: feat(adopt): driven sessions synthesize a draft-born corpus (spec 035)
body:
## Summary

Spec 035, the writing stage of adoption (010 A-2). `src/orchestrator/adopt/synthesis.ts` established, plus the `adopt synthesize <project> --proposal <path-or-hash>` CLI verb (028 D-10).

- **One session per territory, serially (D-1)**, on a provenance-named branch `corpus/synthesis-<hash12>` of the target (D-8); the proposal resolves by path or by journaled `adopt.preflight` content hash, re-hashed on read so an edited proposal refuses (D-9).
- **The guard is code, not prompt text (B-2/B-3):** after every session, the per-session delta is checked against the exported corpus set (D-2/D-4), authored specs must be `status: draft` with `origin.retroactive: true` and establishes edges enumerating the territory's files, and a 037 checker seam is invoked when wired. A violating session's writes are discarded back to the last pinned sha; a passing session is committed by the harness, so every commit on the branch is a guard-passed corpus state (D-5).
- **Territory independence (D-6):** a failed territory is recorded and the rest still run; the report is `failed` unless every territory authored and `spec-spine compile` + `lint` are green inside the target (B-4). The B-5 report names territories, claims, the carried-forward unclaimed paths, sessions, costs, and the branch.
- **Ceilings unchanged (D-7):** day scope folds the project's journal through 033's `evaluateBudget`; run scope reads as this invocation; both checked at spawn boundaries.
- **The corpus set gained `.gitignore` (D-4):** found during this build, `spec-spine compile` writes a non-deterministic `.derived/**/build-meta.json`, which together with the orchestrator's `data/` state root (the tenant-tail lesson) permanently dirties any target that does not ignore them; the scaffold prompt bounds the edit to exactly those two lines.

title: fix(standby): a paused run's queued reverify no longer hot-loops the scan

## Summary

- The sole armed project's recovered run was paused (036's failed daemon build) while its corpus carried both drifted shipped roots (025/028/036 amendments) and new pending work, so the open queued auto-reverifies (026 D-8).

The fix, recorded as 026 D-10: `hasQueuedReverify` answers false unless the run is `"running"`. A queued reverify on a paused run (or on a park that released the slot) is not actionable; its queue entries persist, and the control that lifts the yield already reports through `hasQueuedResume`, whose drive drains the queue immediately after. The scheduler is unchanged except its citation: a cycle with nothing actionable falls through to the standby wait, which keeps the API serving and the pause liftable.

## Testing

title: fix(standby): the amendment probe's run concludes instead of stranding (026 D-9, 021 D-23)
body:
## Summary

The D-8 amendment probe (shipped in #45) opens a project daemon to check for drifted pipeline roots, and that open necessarily journals a fresh run into `running` before the probe ever counts. The zero-queued path then retired the daemon around that run, closing the journals with it still live: the target's latest run read as `running` forever on a project nothing was driving. Found live on tenant-emit, the first fully-adopted corpus the amendment half scanned: its status line claimed a run in flight for 85 minutes with no heartbeat ever journaled.

- `Daemon.concludeIdle()` (021 D-23): the supervisor-facing conclusion for a run that was opened but never driven. It ends the run `completed` through the loop's own idle verdict (the same `run.result` record and journaled transition the nothing-ready branch writes) and refuses unless the run is `running` with no live or failed specExec of its own.
- Standby's zero-queued path (026 D-9) concludes the probe's run before retiring. A refusal means the resumed run carries a pause, a park, or unfinished spec work, all of which only the loop can reconcile, so the probe drives it under the normal flight slot instead of abandoning it.
- A run stranded by a pre-fix probe heals on its next open: recovery resumes it, the probe finds nothing in flight, and it concludes. tenant-emit's stranded run drains at the first scan after the post-merge daemon restart.

Zero-queued settling semantics are otherwise unchanged: a healthy probe still costs no session and no quota.

## Testing

title: feat(api): typed localhost HTTP API and SSE stream (spec 022)
body:
## Summary

Implements spec 022: the daemon's single interface, a loopback-bound `Bun.serve`
API plus a server-sent-events stream, in `src/orchestrator/api/`.

- **Envelope (B-2).** Every JSON answer is `{ok:true,data}` or
  `{ok:false,error:{kind,message}}` with stable kind tokens, so a client
  branches on `ok` and never on an HTTP status alone. `apiVersion` gating is
  opt-in: a request declaring `X-Api-Version` is held to it, one declaring
  nothing is served on the v1 assumption, which keeps plain `curl` a
  first-class client.
- **Reads (B-3).** `/api/dag` (readiness, blockers, pins, invalidation),
  `/api/run`, `/api/quota`, `/api/decisions`, `/api/history`, and
  `/api/evidence/<hash>` (with `?raw=1` for the bytes). Each one is a fold of
  the journal performed during the request: this module holds no state that
  could disagree with a fold (B-6).
- **Events (B-4).** `retry: 3000`, a 15 s comment heartbeat, a 256-event ring
  with `Last-Event-ID` replay (and an explicit gap notice rather than a
  silently incomplete resume). An oversized payload is replaced by a size
  marker, never truncated in place.
- **Controls (B-5).** Run start/pause/resume plus the five per-spec verbs.
  The control record returned is diffed out of the journal, never written
  here: the daemon stays the single author of the fact.
- **Binding (B-1).** Loopback only, refused before the bind, with an
  `authorize` seam so an auth layer slots in front without any shape change.

`api-client.ts` is route-table driven: every path comes from `API_ROUTES` and
every payload type from `types.ts`, so server and client cannot drift without
failing typecheck.

Also fixes a divergence this branch surfaced against current `main`: the
shipped-map fold stopped at the immutable `dag.adopted` record and ignored the
`dag.adopted.refreshed` records spec 021 D-11 introduced. Every re-adopted spec
was reported at its superseded pin, so the node read drifted, entered
`invalidatedSet`, and cascaded a pin-drift blocker onto each dependent;
`/api/dag` answered `nextReady: null` with the whole backlog stalled while the
daemon was still building. It now replays those records exactly as the daemon's
own `computeShippedMap` does, and still appends nothing.

## Testing

- `bun test` green: 298 pass, 0 fail (62 in `src/orchestrator/api/`).
- `bun run typecheck` clean, which is also what proves the real `Daemon`
  satisfies `ControlTarget` with no adapter (asserted at compile time in

- Gate green: `spec-spine compile`, `lint --fail-on-warn`, `index check`,
  `couple --base origin/main --head HEAD` (11 paths, no drift).
- AC-2 checked by hand against a fixture daemon: every read endpoint returns
  the documented envelope under real `curl`, `?raw=1` serves the bytes with
  their own content type, and all seven response types round-trip through the
  typed client. The SSE stream was curled directly to confirm the `retry: 3000`
